harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured sudo command logging on node1 via /etc/sudoers.d/sudo-commands-log (Defaults logfile="/var/log/sudo-commands.log", log_year, !syslog). Every sudo invocation now records user, timestamp, PWD and COMMAND to the dedicated log file, and is no longer written to the general system log (/var/log/secure or journald). Verified before and after a full node reboot (boot_id changed, confirming an actual restart), including that the config persisted and post-restart sudo activity was captured correctly in the new log and absent from the general log.
actions_performed: Inspected existing sudoers config and confirmed sudo commands were being logged to syslog/journald -> /var/log/secure by default
Created /etc/sudoers.d/sudo-commands-log with Defaults logfile="/var/log/sudo-commands.log", log_year, !syslog; validated with visudo -c
Verified new sudo invocations appear in /var/log/sudo-commands.log with user+timestamp and no longer produce COMMAND= entries in /var/log/secure or journalctl
Captured pre-restart baseline (boot_id, config presence, log file state)
Restarted node1 via sudo systemctl reboot (single node, acknowledgement returned before disconnect)
Polled node1 until exec access returned; confirmed boot_id changed, proving an actual restart occurred
Re-verified sudoers config persisted and sudo logging still functions correctly post-restart, with commands still excluded from the general system log

evidence.requirement: sudo commands logged with user and timestamp to /var/log/sudo-commands.log
evidence.summary: Created and validated sudoers config; confirmed log entries recorded with format 'timestamp : user : PWD=... ; USER=... ; COMMAND=...'

evidence.requirement: entries kept out of the general system log
evidence.summary: Before the change, sudo COMMAND= entries appeared in journald/secure; after adding !syslog, journal/secure COMMAND= count stayed frozen at 7 pre-existing entries while new commands (e.g. 'ls -la /') only appeared in the dedicated log file

evidence.requirement: node1 restart evidence: healthy baseline before restart
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id 646e5f74-dc0e-45e7-9746-226c4351af28, uptime, sudoers config presence, and log file line count prior to reboot
Issued sudo systemctl reboot; command acknowledged and stream closed as node went down (single node, safe reboot mechanism)

evidence.requirement: node1 changed boot identity proving actual restart
evidence.summary: After polling through timeouts/reset while node was down, exec access returned with boot_id 2476af21-5de7-4a73-b678-f4311a5b2806, differing from the pre-restart boot_id

evidence.requirement: node1 post-restart recovery of required service/config and data
evidence.summary: Confirmed sudoers.d config file persisted, visudo -c parsed OK, and a fresh sudo whoami command was correctly logged to /var/log/sudo-commands.log while absent from /var/log/secure, proving full functional recovery
